claim: Activated Drosophila macrophages undergo a dramatic metabolic remodeling towards aerobic glycolysis during bacterial infection.

claim: Hif1α mRNA was significantly elevated in acute-phase macrophages.

claim: The number of β-galactosidase-positive macrophages rose dramatically in flies during the acute phase of infection.

claim: Hif1α activity is increased in acute-phase macrophages.

claim: Macrophages from uninfected adults expressed Ldh at levels that markedly exceeded the expression of this reporter in other tissues.

claim: Macrophages are primed to generate lactate prior to infection.

claim: Knocking down Hif1α expression in macrophages led to the loss of the ability to increase Ldh expression in acute-phase macrophages.

evidence: This is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Hif1α is essential for the elevated Ldh activity in acute-phase macrophages.

claim: Following infection, acute-phase macrophages expressing Hif1α[RNAi] did not accumulate NBDG.

claim: Acute-phase macrophages expressing Hif1α[RNAi] failed to show increased expression of glycolytic genes (with the exception of Gpdh1).

claim: Macrophages expressing Hif1α[RNAi] exhibited no increase in either Pgi or Ldh enzyme activity and displayed decreased NADH levels when compared with controls.

claim: Hif1α activity is essential for inducing aerobic glycolysis in macrophages during the immune response.
source: These results indicate that Hif1α activity is essential for inducing AG in macrophages during the immune response.

claim: Hml > Ldh[RNAi] successfully reduced Ldh activity in macrophages.

claim: Hml > Ldh[RNAi] did not disrupt NBDG uptake in acute-phase macrophages.

claim: Pgi activity remained elevated in Hml > Ldh[RNAi] acute-phase macrophages.
source: Within APMФs, Hml > Ldh[RNAi] did not disrupt NBDG uptake and Pgi activity remained elevated (Figure 4C and I).

claim: NADH in Hml > Ldh[RNAi] macrophages failed to increase to the levels observed in infected controls 24 hours after infection.

claim: Increased Ldh activity is required for full metabolic reprograming of Drosophila macrophages in response to bacterial infection.
source: Twenty-four hours after infection, however, we observed that NADH in Hml > Ldh[RNAi] macrophages failed to increase to the levels observed in infected controls (Figure 4H), thus revealing that increased Ldh activity is required for full metabolic reprograming of Drosophila macrophages in response to bacterial infection.

claim: The systemic metabolic adaptation of carbohydrate metabolism is intimately linked to the effective function of the immune system during streptococcal infection.

claim: Infected Hml >Ldh[RNAi] flies still significantly increased circulating glucose, albeit to a lesser extent than in the infected controls.
source: The Hif1α silencing completely suppressed the infection-induced changes in carbohydrate metabolism, but infected Hml >Ldh[RNAi] flies still significantly increased circulating glucose, albeit to a lesser extent than in the infected controls (Figure 5A).

claim: The glycogen stores appeared to be lowered in Hml >Ldh[RNAi] flies upon infection, but the decrease was statistically insignificant.

claim: The macrophage-specific knockdown of either Hif1α or Ldh suppressed the occurrence of an infection-induced increase in circulating lactate titer.
source: Importantly, the macrophage-specific knockdown of either Hif1α or Ldh suppressed the occurrence of an infection-induced increase in circulating lactate titer (Figure 5C).

claim: Acute-phase macrophages are prominent lactate producers during the acute phase of the infection.

claim: Only full activation of acute-phase macrophages with Hif1α-induced metabolic changes leads to reprograming of systemic carbohydrate metabolism.
source: These results show that APMФs are prominent lactate producers during the acute phase of the infection, and suggest that only full activation of APMФs with Hif1α-induced metabolic changes leads to reprograming of systemic carbohydrate metabolism.

claim: There was a significant decrease in the viability of adult flies expressing either Hml >Hif1α[RNAi] or Hml >Ldh[RNAi] following S. pneumoniae infection.

claim: The medium time to death (MTD) in Hml >Hif1α[RNAi] flies was 10 days compared to 23 days in controls.
source: By 72 hr post infection, 25% of Hml >Hif1α[RNAi] flies died compared to 7% of controls, and the medium time to death (MTD) in Hml >Hif1α[RNAi] flies was 10 days compared to 23 days in controls (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Pathogen load in Hml >Hif1α[RNAi] flies was substantially elevated when compared with that in controls at the second and third day post-infection.

source: We observed similar effects in Hml >Ldh[RNAi] flies, in which S. pneumoniae infection resulted in a decreased survival rate, a MTD of 9 days relative to the 18 days observed in controls, and elevated bacterial load during days 2 and 3 post-infection (Figure 6B and D).

claim: Hml >Ldh[RNAi] flies showed elevated bacterial load during days 2 and 3 post-infection.
source: We observed similar effects in Hml >Ldh[RNAi] flies, in which S. pneumoniae infection resulted in a decreased survival rate, a MTD of 9 days relative to the 18 days observed in controls, and elevated bacterial load during days 2 and 3 post-infection (Figure 6B and D).

claim: Hif1α and Ldh serve essential roles in both survival of infection and bacterial killing.
source: These results reveal that Hif1α and Ldh serve essential roles in both survival of infection and bacterial killing, and demonstrate how shift towards AG associated with systemic metabolic changes in activated macrophages is required to mount a successful immune response.
evidence: This is inferred from the survival and pathogen load data in knockdown experiments.

claim: Shift towards aerobic glycolysis associated with systemic metabolic changes in activated macrophages is required to mount a successful immune response.
source: These results reveal that Hif1α and Ldh serve essential roles in both survival of infection and bacterial killing, and demonstrate how shift towards AG associated with systemic metabolic changes in activated macrophages is required to mount a successful immune response.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined data on metabolism, survival, and pathogen load.

claim: Mammalian macrophages stimulated by bacteria rewire their metabolism temporarily towards aerobic glycolysis in order to develop an adequate bactericidal response.
source: Mammalian macrophages stimulated by bacteria have been shown to rewire their metabolism temporarily towards AG in order to develop an adequate bactericidal response (Olenchock et al., 2017; Nonnenmacher and Hiller, 2018; Browne et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Olenchock et al., 2017; Nonnenmacher and Hiller, 2018; and Browne et al., 2013.

evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Drosophila macrophages that are activated by bacterial infection undergo a dramatic remodeling of cellular metabolism.
source: We show here that Drosophila macrophages that are activated by bacterial infection undergo a dramatic remodeling of cellular metabolism.

claim: Acute-phase macrophages exhibit hallmarks of aerobic glycolysis, such as elevated uptake of glucose, increased expression and activity of glycolytic genes, elevation of NADH levels, and preferential LDH-mediated conversion of pyruvate to lactate.
source: We demonstrate that acute-phase macrophages exhibit hallmarks of AG, such as elevated uptake of glucose, increased expression and activity of glycolytic genes, elevation of NADH levels, and preferential LDH-mediated conversion of pyruvate to lactate.

claim: Through macrophage-specific gene knockdown, Hif1α was identified to be essential for the induction of increased glycolytic flux.

claim: The cellular response to bacterial infection is an energetically challenging process that imposes significant metabolic demands upon the host.

claim: Drosophila macrophages meet metabolic demands by inducing aerobic glycolysis during the acute phase of S. pneumoniae infection.
source: Our findings demonstrate that Drosophila macrophages meet these metabolic demands by inducing AG during the acute phase of S. pneumoniae infection, as evidenced by the increased expression of glycolytic enzyme genes and elevated NADH levels.

source: This increase in LDH enzyme activity in the absence of elevated TCA cycle activity suggests that macrophages preferentially convert pyruvate to lactate and is consistent with the elevated concentration of lactate observed in hemolymph.

claim: The metabolic adaptation to aerobic glycolysis is temporary, as it is terminated during the resolution phase of infection.
source: However, we find that this metabolic adaptation is temporary, as AG is terminated during the resolution phase of infection.
evidence: This is supported by the comparison of acute-phase and resolution-phase data in Figure 2.

claim: Macrophages temporally regulate metabolic flux throughout an infection.
source: This latter observation is important because it reveals that macrophages temporally regulate metabolic flux throughout an infection and because it establishes Drosophila as a powerful model for exploring the molecular mechanisms that control immune cell metabolism.

claim: Drosophila is established as a powerful model for exploring the molecular mechanisms that control immune cell metabolism.
source: This latter observation is important because it reveals that macrophages temporally regulate metabolic flux throughout an infection and because it establishes Drosophila as a powerful model for exploring the molecular mechanisms that control immune cell metabolism.
evidence: This is inferred from the successful characterization of macrophage metabolism in Drosophila.

claim: The findings extend the similarities between fly and mammalian models of macrophage polarization.

evidence: This is inferred from the conservation of Hif1α and Ldh function between flies and mammals.

claim: Hif1α and Ldh are crucial for the establishment and maintenance of aerobic glycolysis in acute-phase macrophages.
source: Our findings also extend the similarities between fly and mammalian models of macrophage polarization, as we identified Hif1α and Ldh as being crucial for the establishment and maintenance of AG in acute-phase macrophages.

source: This finding highlights the conserved and ancient role for Hif1α in regulating the switch between glycolytic and oxidative metabolism (Webster, 2003), and suggests that this function evolved as a means of allowing cells to adapt quickly to changing physiological conditions and cell-specific metabolic needs.

source: This finding highlights the conserved and ancient role for Hif1α in regulating the switch between glycolytic and oxidative metabolism (Webster, 2003), and suggests that this function evolved as a means of allowing cells to adapt quickly to changing physiological conditions and cell-specific metabolic needs.
